items.title: Staged Access and Liability for Dual-Use Artificial Intelligence
items.desc: Models how regulators should combine staged release of dual-use AI models with developer liability, showing how liability induces more defensive search for flaws after release. [NBER, issued 2026-08-10]

items.title: AI Agents and Prompt Engineering in Econometric Coding
items.desc: Studies how large language models write econometric code, comparing performance across statistical software, zero- vs few-shot prompting, and degrees of agentic autonomy. [NBER, issued 2026-08-10]

items.title: Environmental and Economic Implications of Artificial Intelligence Data Centers in the United States
items.desc: Uses electricity demand growth, cooling requirements, and backup-system operation to evaluate the environmental and economic impacts of U.S. AI data centers, finding impacts depend on grid context, not just facility design. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-10]

items.title: Beyond Headcount and Human Capital: The Effective Cognitive Population as a Decomposable Capacity Unit for AI-Era Planning
items.desc: Proposes an 'Effective Cognitive Population' measure that extends headcount- and human-capital-based national planning to count AI systems as decomposable units of cognitive capacity. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-10]

items.title: AI and the Research Team
items.desc: A span-of-control model reconciles why AI is associated with larger research teams overall, yet lets solo mathematicians produce research-grade results: AI lowers execution costs and automates codifiable tasks. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-09]

items.title: From Product Search to Preference Articulation: The Economics of Agentic Commerce
items.desc: Compares manual product search with agentic search in which consumers delegate discovery to AI agents that screen broad catalogs through noisy preference representations, deriving implications for digital commerce. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-08-09]

items.title: A Fair Objective for Human-Empowerment-Preserving AI: Desiderata, Design, and Likely Behavioral Consequences
items.desc: Game-theoretic analysis of AI agents explicitly designed to preserve human empowerment and manage the power balance in human-AI interactions. [arXiv econ.TH/cs.GT, posted 2026-08-08]

items.title: Reading Copom's Tone: A Weighted LLM Framework for Hawkish-Dovish Sentiment, Forward Guidance, and Uncertainty
items.desc: An LLM-based NLP framework that classifies sentences of Brazilian central bank (Copom) statements as hawkish, dovish, or neutral to measure policy tone, forward guidance, and uncertainty. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-07]

items.title: Measuring Concept Content in Text from LLM Activations: ESG Evidence from Concept Vectors and Linear Probes
items.desc: Moves beyond dictionary and embedding measures of text content by reading concept intensity (e.g., ESG themes) directly from LLM internal activations via concept vectors and linear probes. [arXiv econ.GN cross-list, posted 2026-08-07]

items.title: Tabular Foundation Models and the Unity of Economic Behaviour
items.desc: Runs a unified choice experiment spanning risk, time, losses, valuation, and social preferences, and shows a frozen tabular foundation model can recover a person's hidden choices in one domain from their behaviour in others. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-07]

items.title: Joint Lyapunov Certificates for K-Agent Generative AI Governance: Stochastic Stability, Emergent Ensemble Risk, and Zero-Knowledge Governance Attestation
items.desc: Develops a mathematical model-risk-management framework for governing systems of coupled self-adapting generative AI models, with stability certificates and governance attestation. [arXiv q-fin.RM, posted 2026-08-10]

items.title: Telemetry and Concealment in Self-Adapting Generative AI: Logging Architecture, Adversarial Model Hiding, and the Limits of Detection
items.desc: Argues model-risk-management guidance built for static model lifecycles breaks down for continually self-adapting generative AI, and analyzes logging architectures and the limits of detecting adversarial model changes. [arXiv q-fin.RM, posted 2026-08-10]

items.title: Hybrid Neural-Classical Correction for Frozen Time Series Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Ablation Study on High-Frequency Stock Prediction
items.desc: Ablation study showing how hybrid neural-classical correction layers adapt frozen time-series foundation models, which generalize well zero-shot but underperform on high-frequency finance. [arXiv q-fin.ST, posted 2026-08-09]

items.title: Can Open-Weight Models Compete on Financial Text Comprehension?
items.desc: Updates the Financial Touchstone benchmark (2,967 question-context-answer items) to test whether open-weight LLMs from Chinese labs match proprietary frontier models on real-world financial text tasks. [arXiv q-fin.GN, posted 2026-08-09]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: The Impact of Manipulated Clinical Decision Support Algorithm on Opioid Prescribing Decision
items.desc: Management Science study of how a manipulated clinical decision-support algorithm shifts physicians' opioid prescribing decisions, with implications for governing algorithmic advice in healthcare operations. [Management Science, published online 2026-08-10]

items.title: Fighting Fire with Fire: Infusing Artificial Intelligence into Peer Review to Sustain Quality Scholarship
items.desc: Proposes infusing AI into the peer-review process to sustain scholarship quality as AI-assisted submissions grow; published alongside three invited commentaries in the same issue. [Management Science, published online 2026-08-07]

items.title: Learning to Simulate from Heavy-Tailed Distribution via Diffusion Model
items.desc: Develops diffusion-model-based generators for simulating heavy-tailed distributions, extending deep generative AI methods to stochastic simulation in operations research. [Operations Research, published online 2026-08-10]

items.title: Certifiable Deep Importance Sampling for Rare-Event Simulation of Black Box Systems
items.desc: Presents deep-learning-driven importance sampling with certifiable guarantees for rare-event simulation of black-box systems, relevant to risk and reliability analysis in operations. [Operations Research, published online 2026-08-07]

items.title: Wall St. Wants Another Half-Trillion Dollars for the A.I. Boom
items.desc: Wall Street lenders are lining up roughly another half-trillion dollars of debt financing for AI infrastructure tied to Nvidia-powered data centers, deepening the financial system's exposure to the AI buildout. [NYT, 2026-08-10]

items.title: A.I.-Driven Chip Crunch Leads to New Rush of Lobbying in Washington
items.desc: An AI-driven memory-chip shortage is rippling through electronics supply chains and has set off a lobbying scramble in Washington over chip allocation. [NYT, 2026-08-10]

items.title: Why Meta Is Betting Big on Open A.I.
items.desc: DealBook analysis of the business economics behind Meta's release of an open version of its most powerful AI model and what open-weight strategy means for the AI market. [NYT DealBook, 2026-08-10]
